newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico faces sorghum commercialization woes - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mexico faces sorghum commercialization woes - paper.

text.p: Differences over price are threatening the commercialization of Mexico's sorghum crop in the northern state of Tamaulipas, daily Reforma reported Wednesday.

Citing unnamed sources in the National Hog Farming Council, Reforma said sorghum growers in the state, which is on the verge of starting to harvest, are demanding 1,600 pesos per tonne whereas consumers are offering 1,100 pesos.
"They are pushing for prices beyond all trade context because international prices have dropped and they are the basis of domestic pricing levels," one council member told the daily.

Tamaulipas sorghum farmers severely criticized the government last year for allowing imports from Argentina which also caused a sharp dip in internal prices. The northeastern state is the top sorghum growing area in Mexico.
Farmers expect a crop between 1.5 to 1.8 million tonnes. The Agriculture Ministry estimates the state will produce 2 million tonnes of sorghum.
